topics: Enzyme-Substrate Complex Intermediate ($E + S \rightleftharpoons ES \rightarrow E + P$)
Michaelis Constant ($K_m$) as an Inverse Affinity Metric
quickSummary: Under steady-state kinetics, initial velocity follows the Michaelis-Menten equation: v0 = Vmax[S] / (Km + [S]). Vmax is the maximum reaction rate at enzyme saturation. Km is the substrate concentration at half-maximal velocity (v0 = 1/2 Vmax) and serves as an inverse measure of substrate affinity (lower Km = higher affinity). kcat is the turnover number per active site, and kcat/Km measures catalytic efficiency. Lineweaver-Burk double reciprocal plots linearize kinetics to determine exact Km and Vmax.

conceptBreakdown.heading: 7. The Michaelis-Menten Kinetic Model
conceptBreakdown.title: 7. The Michaelis-Menten Kinetic Model

summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: v0 = Vmax[S] / (Km + [S]). Km is the substrate concentration at 1/2 Vmax (lower Km = higher affinity). Lineweaver-Burk x-intercept is -1/Km; y-intercept is 1/Vmax.

conceptBreakdown.content:
Enzyme reactions proceed through an intermediate **Enzyme-Substrate (ES)** complex:
$$E + S \underset{k_{-1}}{\overset{k_1}{\rightleftharpoons}} ES \xrightarrow{k_{\text{cat}}} E + P$$

### The Michaelis-Menten Equation
$$\Large \mathbf{v_0 = \frac{V_{\max} [S]}{K_m + [S]}}$$

• **$V_{\max}$ (Maximum Velocity)**: Velocity achieved when all active sites are completely saturated with substrate ($[S] \gg K_m$).
• **$K_m$ (Michaelis Constant)**: Substrate concentration at which initial velocity equals half of maximum velocity ($v_0 = \frac{1}{2}V_{\max}$).
  - **Affinity Indicator**: $K_m$ is **inversely proportional to affinity**. A low $K_m$ indicates strong substrate affinity; a high $K_m$ indicates weak affinity.
• **$k_{\text{cat}}$ (Turnover Number)**: Maximum substrate molecules transformed per active site per second ($k_{\text{cat}} = \frac{V_{\max}}{[E]_T}$).
• **Catalytic Efficiency**: Ratio $\frac{k_{\text{cat}}}{K_m}$.

conceptBreakdown.heading: 7.1 Lineweaver-Burk Double-Reciprocal Plot
conceptBreakdown.title: 7.1 Lineweaver-Burk Double-Reciprocal Plot
conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
LINEWEAVER-BURK DOUBLE RECIPROCAL PLOT
                       
           1/v₀ ▲
                │      / Slope = K_m / V_max
                │     /
                │    /
    1/V_max ────┼───/
                │  /
  ──┴───────────┼─/────────────────► 1/[S]
 -1/K_m         │
conceptBreakdown.content:
Taking the double reciprocal of the Michaelis-Menten equation linearizes the hyperbolic saturation curve ($y = mx + c$):
$$\Large \mathbf{\frac{1}{v_0} = \left( \frac{K_m}{V_{\max}} \right) \frac{1}{[S]} + \frac{1}{V_{\max}}}$$

• **y-intercept** $= \frac{1}{V_{\max}}$
• **x-intercept** $= -\frac{1}{K_m}$
• **Slope** $= \frac{K_m}{V_{\max}}$
